question: AFL/AFLW sources with live in-play score, period and clock
note: Researcher output plus one skeptic per class plus a completeness critic. Labels as returned; a claim whose skeptic verdict is not confirmed carries that verdict. Documentation-only: no live AFLW payload was read.

searched: fitzRoy R source on GitHub (R/womens_stats.R, R/helpers-afl.R) and the pkgdown vignettes (womens-stats, Introduction to fitzRoy), plus search highlights for R/fetch-results.R-adjacent code and fitzRoy issue #203

fitzRoy-ts: issues #145 and #148 (read in full), PR #147, issue #179, repo README and docs/cli.md (search highlights only), and jackemcpherson.com/docs/afl-data-ecosystem.md (first 16000 chars fetched, rest via highlights)
Stack Overflow 42380683 (2017 question about the afl.com.au token endpoint)

www.afl.com.au pages: terms-of-use (full text), mobile/terms (full), contact-us, licensing-queries, policies, privacy (search highlight), robots.txt, rss, rss/rssview, aflw/matches/9081, get-the-afl-app/features, AFLW Grand Final timings article; womens.afl root; two guessed Non-Broadcast Rights Holders URLs (not found)
App Store listing for AFLW Official App, Telstra support page 'What is the AFL Live App', AppBrain listing (all via Exa search highlights)

AFL Regulations PDFs (2025 and 2026, table of contents and one definition only), AFL's 30 Nov 2012 ALRC submission with its 2012 Media Accreditation annexure, AFL CEO statement of 2015-08-18 (Exa search highlights)

12 Exa searches: fitzRoy-ts AFLW/matchClock; official statements on third-party API use; AFL data licensing; AFLW live match centre; fitzRoy-ts AflApiClient source; official RSS/widget/embed; fitzRoy disclaimer/permission text; AFLW app features; Non-Broadcast Rights Holders; Telstra Media data licensing; AFL Regulations clause 29.4 (twice)

candidates.name: AFL website CFS API (api.afl.com.au/cfs/afl/..., token from POST WMCTok)
candidates.kind: AFL's own website data API, token-gated and undocumented. NOT called by this session. Live fields are reported by third parties for AFL men's only; no AFLW live observation exists anywhere I read. Enumerations below describe AFLW.
candidates.accessModel: Token-gated but keyless: third-party code POSTs https://api.afl.com.au/cfs/afl/WMCTok (no key, no login), then sends the returned token in header x-media-mis-token. No docs, SLA or terms page for this API found. A 2017 third-party post says the token rotates every 24 hours. Per ADR-004 this endpoint is outside the accepted scope.
candidates.cost: No price published; no fee or key in any third-party code read.

claims.text: The fitzRoy R source (deprecated get_aflw_* functions in R/womens_stats.R) contains calls to the CFS season and matchItems/round endpoints with AFLW ids. AFLW ids carry the infix 264: season CD_S{year}264, round CD_R{year}264{NN}, match CD_M{year}264{NNNN}. Men's ids in the other sources read here carry 014 (see c1-men-score). This is source code, not an observed AFLW payload, and is silent on live play.
claims.label: verified-read
claims.quote: meta_url <- paste0( "http://api.afl.com.au/cfs/afl/season?seasonId=CD_S", years[[i]], "264" ) ... # Match ID: "CD_M20172640101" # Round ID: "CD_R201726401" M->R, last two characters removed # Competition ID: "CD_S2017264" R->S, last two characters removed
claims.skepticNote: Re-read raw womens_stats.R: the season URL ending "264", the "CD_M20172640101 / CD_R201726401 / CD_S2017264" comments and the matchItems/round call are all there and the quote is verbatim. Small imprecision: only get_aflw_cookie() and get_aflw_match_data() carry the deprecated badge; get_aflw_rounds, get_aflw_round_data and get_aflw_detailed_data are plain @export (fitzRoy NEWS.md says get_aflw_cookie remains deprecated). The URLs are http://, not https. The 264 infix also matches the aflapi providerId CD_M20262641601 in the local 2026-11-27 captures.

claims.text: A fitzRoy vignette prints the structure of CFS matchItems for AFLW 2020 round 1 (completed matches, fetch_results comp='AFLW'): status CONCLUDED, scoreWorm NA, and per-period score and clock tables of 4 rows x 5 columns per match. This is a captured structure of COMPLETED AFLW matches only (the 4x5 column names are not shown in the text read). The vignette build date is unknown; the last three segments came from a search highlight because the page fetch was cut at 14000 characters.
claims.label: third-party-report
claims.quote: #> $ round.competitionId <chr> "CD_S2020264", "CD_S2020264", "CD_… ... #> $ status <chr> "CONCLUDED", "CONCLUDED", "CONCLUD… ... #> $ scoreWorm <lgl> NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA ... #> $ homeTeamScore.periodScore <list> [<data.frame[4 x 5]>], [<data.fram… ... #> $ matchClock.periods <list> [<data.frame[4 x 5]>], [<data.fram…
claims.skepticNote: Full-page fetch (60000 chars, not the 14000 cut) reproduces every quoted glimpse line: round.competitionId CD_S2020264, status CONCLUDED, scoreWorm NA (scoreMap also NA), homeTeamScore.periodScore and matchClock.periods as 4 x 5 data.frames. Completed-only is guaranteed by construction: fitzRoy R/fetch-results.R filters match.status == "CONCLUDED" before this output. No live content possible in this vignette.

claims.text: fitzroy-ts (a third-party library over the AFL API) documents the live fields it surfaces: a score-level status string (LIVE, QTR_TIME, HALF_TIME, 3QTR_TIME, FULL_TIME), matchClockPeriods and a derived completedQuarter 0-4, and says the upstream status strings regressed in 2026 so completedQuarter should be preferred. Quarter scores q1Home..q4Away are in the same type. Men's-oriented documentation; AFLW live use not shown.
claims.label: third-party-report
claims.quote: livePeriodStatus: string | null; // afl-api score-level status: LIVE, QTR_TIME, HALF_TIME, 3QTR_TIME, FULL_TIME (raw upstream string) // v3.1.0 live-match fields: prefer completedQuarter over livePeriodStatus // for break/siren detection (the upstream status strings regressed in 2026) matchClockPeriods: ReadonlyArray<MatchClockPeriod> | null; completedQuarter: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | null;
claims.skepticNote: Quote is verbatim in the saved doc (livePeriodStatus comment, the 'prefer completedQuarter ... regressed in 2026' comment, matchClockPeriods, completedQuarter). Third-party library type definitions, men's-oriented, no AFLW live use shown, as the researcher said.

claims.text: The same third-party document tabulates the 'afl-api' source as covering AFLW 2017+ and as best for 'Live scores'. This is a claim in a table with no AFLW live capture, test or sample shown anywhere I read.
claims.label: third-party-report
claims.quote: | `afl-api` | AFLM 2012+, AFLW 2017+, VFL/VFLW 2021+ | Live scores, official data, multi-competition |
claims.skepticNote: Table row is verbatim: afl-api | AFLM 2012+, AFLW 2017+, VFL/VFLW 2021+ | Live scores, official data, multi-competition. It is a coverage-and-purpose table, not a capture. It does not say which host 'afl-api' means: fitzroy-ts uses CFS matchItems (issues #145 and #179) and fitzRoy R also uses aflapi v2 for fixtures. The local 2026-11-27 GF captures show aflapi v2 live items with status LIVE and no score, so 'Live scores' cannot be pinned to any single host for AFLW. 'third-party-report' is the right label.

claims.text: AFL MEN'S, not AFLW: a fitzRoy-ts issue reports (observed live 2026-06-13, Melbourne v Essendon, CD_M20260141403) that the CFS matchItems payload carries score.status and score.matchClock.periods[] with periodNumber, periodSeconds, periodCompleted, periodStart, nextPeriodStart. The sample shows one COMPLETED period (periodSeconds 1786); it does not show a running clock for a period in progress.
claims.label: third-party-report
claims.quote: "score": { "status": "LIVE", "matchClock": { "periods": [ { "periodNumber": 1, "periodSeconds": 1786, "periodCompleted": true, "periodStart": null, "nextPeriodStart": "2026-06-13T03:51:15.000+0000" } ] }, … }
claims.skepticNote: Issue #145 body reproduces the score.status LIVE / matchClock.periods JSON verbatim, for CD_M20260141403 (Melbourne v Essendon, men's), created 2026-06-13T03:56Z. One COMPLETED period only (periodSeconds 1786, periodCompleted true); no running clock shown. Labelled men's by the researcher; nothing here is AFLW.

claims.text: AFL MEN'S, not AFLW: the same issue shows the library's normalised output mid-Q1 with live point totals and Q1 goals/behinds, so the CFS item carried a live score in play for that men's match (the output is fitzroy's transform, not the raw CFS body).
claims.label: third-party-report
claims.quote: "matchId": "CD_M20260141403", "status": "Live", "livePeriodStatus": "LIVE", "homePoints": 34, "awayPoints": 16, "q1Home": { "goals": 5, "behinds": 4, "points": 34 }, ... This was 5+ minutes past the real-world QT siren.
claims.skepticNote: The quote is verbatim, but the claim text says 'mid-Q1 with live point totals'. The issue says the output was taken 'at Q1' and '5+ minutes past the real-world QT siren', and homePoints 34 / awayPoints 16 equal the q1Home / q1Away points with q2 null. That is a score present during the quarter-time break while status read LIVE, not an in-play running score. Men's only, and fitzroy's transform output rather than the raw CFS body, which the researcher did say. Rating unaffected (liveScore stays not-determined for AFLW).

claims.text: AFL MEN'S, not AFLW: the issue reports score.status stuck on LIVE through quarter breaks in 2026 while periodCompleted flipped within seconds of each siren. No update interval for the endpoint itself is stated anywhere I read.
claims.label: third-party-report
claims.quote: it stays on `LIVE` from bounce through full-time, with only `FULL_TIME` / `CONCLUDED` flipping after the final siren. ... `periodCompleted` flips to `true` within seconds of each siren.
claims.skepticNote: Both quoted sentences are in #145 verbatim. 'periodCompleted flips within seconds of each siren' is the issue author's assertion (repeated in PR #147), from one men's match on 2026-06-13; no endpoint refresh interval is stated anywhere I read, as the researcher said.

claims.text: How third parties reach the CFS API: a POST to the WMCTok path returns a token, which is then sent as header x-media-mis-token. Source code only; I did not call it.
claims.label: verified-read
claims.quote: get_afl_cookie <- function() { response <- httr::POST("https://api.afl.com.au/cfs/afl/WMCTok", fitzroy_ua()) # nolint httr::content(response)$token } ... httr::add_headers("x-media-mis-token" = cookie)
claims.tool: mcp__Exa__web_fetch_exa + mcp__Exa__web_search_exa (highlights, same file via github.com blob)
claims.skepticNote: helpers-afl.R at main: get_afl_cookie POSTs https://api.afl.com.au/cfs/afl/WMCTok with only a user agent and returns content$token; fetch_* functions send it as x-media-mis-token. Verbatim. Source code only, as the researcher said. The womens-stats vignette adds 'Often this gets changed or moved and without it, the code won't work', a stability note the researcher did not capture.

claims.text: A 2017 Stack Overflow answer says the token response from the older www.afl.com.au/api/cfs/afl/WMCTok path carried a 'disclaimer' field with Telstra copyright wording; the asker also says the token changes every 24 hours. Third-party, 2017, older host path, not observed now. Quoted only; no assessment (Rule 45).
claims.label: third-party-report
claims.quote: content(token)$disclaimer #[1] "All content and material contained within this site is protected by copyright owned by or licensed to Telstra. Unauthorised reproduction, publishing, transmission, distribution, copying or other use is prohibited.
claims.skepticNote: Stack Overflow 42380683 (2017-02-22): the answer's code reads http://www.afl.com.au/api/cfs/afl/WMCTok and prints the $disclaimer string verbatim as quoted (the source also lacks a closing quotation mark). The asker, not the answerer, says the token 'is updated every 24 hrs'. Third-party, 2017, older www host path; quoted only, no assessment (Rule 45).

claims.text: Our own ADR-004 lists this endpoint as outside the accepted scope, so any use of CFS is a new Rule 45 question for the owner, not covered by the aflapi acceptance.
claims.label: verified-read
claims.quote: - Any other aflapi field, endpoint or write of aflapi data beyond the rows above (player data, statistics, per-quarter scores, lineups) ... - The CFS endpoint (`api.afl.com.au/cfs`, token-gated) or any other AFL host
claims.skepticNote: Read the ADR-004 file: line 75 and line 77 match the quote. Missed implication: line 77 reads 'The CFS endpoint (api.afl.com.au/cfs, token-gated) or any other AFL host', so the exclusion also reaches www.afl.com.au (candidate 2), the RSS feed (4) and the apps (3), not just CFS.

openQuestions: Does CFS carry score, status and matchClock.periods DURING an AFLW match? No AFLW live capture, test fixture or report was found. Settles it: a capture during an AFLW match (next season about Aug 2027), only if the owner's Rule 45 review covers CFS, or an answer from the AFL.
Is periodSeconds a running clock for the period in progress, or only the length of completed periods? The one live sample (men's, #145) shows a completed period only.

Is scoreWorm populated live for AFLW? fitzRoy issue #203 (2023-08-01, men's id CD_M20230141903, search highlight) says score.scoreWorm and score.matchClock exist on /cfs/afl/matchItem/{id}; the AFLW 2020 vignette shows scoreWorm NA on round items.

Is the aflapi v2 providerId the CFS id? The Grand Final's aflapi providerId CD_M20262641601 (from the 2026-11-22 evidence file, not re-read) fits the CFS AFLW pattern CD_M{year}264..., but this is a pattern inference, untested.

A 2021 R Journal article (third-party) says fitzRoy once lost AFLW data because it 'was removed from official AFL media'; AFLW availability on the AFL site's data endpoints has changed before. The 2026 status regressions (#145, #148) show vocabulary drift. Stability risk, not quantified.
Which document, if any, governs CFS use is not established: no page read names api.afl.com.au. Flagged for human review (Rule 45); no assessment made.

The same page says a licence is required: 'You must be licensed to access the AFLW league and its matches.' The match endpoint is where the vendor documents status.period/periodSecs/periodDisplay (see cd-api-3), so AFLW period and clock are documented by implication only, not shown in any AFLW payload.

classes.researcherDisclosure: READ-ONLY. No repository file edited, created or committed. Local reads: the three outbox files via Read (aflw-source-read-20261122.md lines 1-129 and 204-253 only, the rest of its 316 lines not read; precedents file lines 1-211 of 278, plus two Greps; ADR-004 in full). No call to aflapi.afl.com.au or api.afl.com.au, no token, key or login acquired or used, no sign-up, no POST to any target host. I did not call TheSportsDB with the free key 123, The Odds API with the project's key, or any vendor API. About 33 Exa tool calls (roughly 20 searches, 13 fetch calls, 5 of which failed with 503, CRAWL_EMPTY_CONTENT or returned only nav links; the tool's own error text says 'Error POSTing to endpoint', which is Exa's backend, not a request to a target). Pages fetched in full by Exa: api.squiggle.com.au (1), www.thesportsdb.com (docs_api_data, pricing: 2), jackemcpherson.com (1), sportsapi.app (aussie-rules, pricing, terms, livescores md: 4), the-odds-api.com (terms: 1 ok, 1 failed), www.sofascore.com (1, nav only); failed: api-sports.io (1), datasportsapi.com (2 URLs), glama.ai (1, 503; one earlier fetch of the same host succeeded in the first batch), www.goalserve.com (1). Most other evidence came from Exa search highlights, which are cached excerpts of unknown date; excerpts can omit text, so an absence in them is not proof. html_probe (Cloudflare Worker IP) GETs: api-sports.io/sports/afl (HTTP 403 challenge), www.sofascore.com/terms-and-conditions (HTTP 403), www.goalserve.com/en/terms-and-conditions (HTTP 200, 3000 chars of text). Pages seen only incidentally in search results and NOT investigated (other classes): Sportradar Australian Rules API (developer.sportradar.com: 'We cover both Men’s and Women’s AFL.', match_status e.g. 1st_quarter, timeline match_clock, behind a key) and Data Sports Group (datasportsgroup.com/coverage/australian-football: 'Coverage of AFL Premiership, AFLW & State Leagues'). Rule 45: all terms text is quoted for a human to judge; nothing here certifies a source or assesses legality. Constraint exceptions: none known; whitespace was collapsed in a few quotes (marked)."

ranking.name: Champion Data AFL Sports Data API (B)
ranking.why: Strongest on the claim text, not on labels. Labels are a three-way tie: B rates aflwCoverage, liveScore, livePeriod and liveClock all 'claimed-only', exactly as C and D rate Sportradar and C rates DataSportsAPI. I break the tie on what the documents say. This is the only candidate whose own docs address AFLW live behaviour at field level. cd-api-2: 'AFLW is now formally supported ... past, live and future matches as they happen' (2024-10-25). cd-api-1: AFLW is league 3 and supported by all match endpoints. cd-api-3 and cd-api-5: match status has period, periodSecs, periodDisplay and remainingSecs. cd-api-4: score fields. cd-sbx-3: the vendor says AFLW's shorter quarters do not align with its timing table. Further support: A c5-official-stats shows Champion Data is the AFL Official Statistician per the 11 Feb 2026 Regulations, and B-verifier adds the v1.60 note that Statistics Flow 'supports live match updates' for AFL and AFLW. Weaknesses: no AFLW payload anywhere (the cd-api-3 sample is 2019 men's and internally inconsistent). The clock is poll-only (cd-api-5). R docs describe a 1200 s countdown (a 20-minute quarter), so AFLW 17-minute behaviour is open. The sandbox AFLW replay is contested (cd-sbx-2 vs cd-sbx-3). Statements are 2024 to 2025 vintage, and I found no 2026 AFLW-specific one.
ranking.ownerNeeds: A Champion Data licence that covers AFLW (league 3): cd-api-1 'You must be licensed to access the AFLW league'. The vendor's own access statement is cd-api-6, 'restricted to AFL accredited organisations', not self-serve. An order form (cd-api-7: Transactional tier, Talent packages and a per-gender order form for trial matches; no AFLW package name found). An OAuth2 user or M2M (Auth0) account. The price is unpublished (cd-api-9), usage is 50,000 requests/day and 20/s (cd-api-8), and API terms are not public (cd-api-10). SNS would need an organisation subscription and an AWS endpoint (cd-sns-3), and it is a refresh trigger only (cd-sns-1) with AFLW unnamed (cd-sns-4). Whether Champion Data will license this owner at all, and on what terms, is a human Rule 45 question. No legal assessment made.
ranking.cheapestProbe: Without a licence: one service-desk ticket (B-verifier says only a name and email are needed) asking whether the match endpoint populates status.period, periodSecs, periodDisplay, remainingSecs and score during live AFLW (league 3) matches, and whether the sandbox AFLW replay still exists. That answer settles cd-sbx-2 vs cd-sbx-3 in writing. With a licensed account, the one authenticated probe is a sandbox read (api.afl-sandbox.championdata.io, documented in cd-sbx-6) that lists matches and looks for a league-3 replay, then reads that match. Assertion: status.periodDisplay matches /^Q[1-4] [0-5][0-9]:[0-5][0-9]$/ and the score fields are non-null while the replay is 'live', committed as JSON. A replay shows field behaviour, not production AFLW timing.

ranking.name: Sportradar Australian Rules Football API (C, D)
ranking.why: Tied on labels with rank 1 and rank 3 (all four fields 'claimed-only' in C and D), so this ordering is judgement. For: the vendor says it collects the data itself (my read of the overview: 'collected via Sportradar on-venue scouts and in-house operators'). It documents SR5 (match_status such as 1st_quarter, period_scores 1st_period to 3rd_pause, event period and period_name), SR4 (live scoring, 1 s cache) and SR2 (competition name 'AFL, Women'). Against: SR1's AFLW wording is generic ('We cover both Men's and Women's AFL'). Per-event coverage.scores is 'live' or 'post' (SR3) and the Coverage Matrix that would show AFLW's level is JS-rendered and unread by C and D. Every example on the docs pages is men's AFL (C-verifier). The clock exists only on timeline events 'when available' (SR6, D sr-5), and C-verifier infers it may be cumulative match time, not a per-quarter clock. It sits below rank 1 because the AFLW-live statement is generic rather than AFLW-specific. DataSportsAPI's AFLW claim is more direct but its provenance is weaker, so the 2 vs 3 margin is thin.
ranking.ownerNeeds: A Sportradar developer account. A trial is documented as self-serve (SR8): 30 days, 1,000 requests per rolling 30 days, 1 QPS. The trial terms bar commercial use and publication or display (SR9, quote only). Production needs a signed Order Form that defines the permitted 'Properties' (SR10, D sr-9). Push feeds cannot be self-provisioned, and the price is unpublished. C-verifier also surfaces clause 2.10 (no gambling or betting use without approval) and a 'powered by' requirement. The relay holds only a UFL trial account (D sr-10, expiry assumed), and whether it has an Aussie Rules product is unchecked. All of this goes to a human for a Rule 45 decision. No assessment made.
ranking.cheapestProbe: No key: read the Coverage Matrix row for 'AFL, Women' via a GitHub Actions Playwright runner (CI-as-proxy, per the repo's own rule), because the static read returns 0 rows (C, D). Commit a manifest with the live/post scores flag, play-by-play and clock availability. With an owner-obtained trial key: one request against a completed 2026 AFLW fixture (the Grand Final or a 2026 round match), asserting sport_event.coverage.sport_event_properties.scores == 'live', and that the timeline carries period_name and match_clock. That is one of the 1,000 trial requests. It settles coverage level, not live timing.

ranking.name: DataSportsAPI / SportsAPI (C, E; operator identity unresolved)
ranking.why: Also 'claimed-only' on all four fields. It has the most directly matching claim: DS1 and sa-1 say AFL Women with 'live scores by quarter', DS3 gives quarter scores in points, and sa-2 says clock, score by period and status. Also, a free key reads live data. Weaknesses are provenance and maturity. The aussie-rules sport launched 2026-11-20 (DS2), and my read of openapi.json shows version 2026-11-27 and a Free plan of 100 requests/day, but the first 12,000 characters reached only info and tags, not any aussie-rules schema. The upstream is unnamed (DS7, sa-8). The page says the source 'keeps hardly anything but scores' (DS3). Clock is null when the source keeps none and aussie rules is not named as a running or stop clock (DS5, sa-3).
